subject: ent
title: Snoring and obstructive sleep apnoea

steps.tx: **Snoring** vibrates relaxed pharyngeal soft tissues (soft palate, uvula, tonsillar pillars) during sleep; **obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA)** adds repetitive complete (apnoea) or partial (hypopnoea) upper airway collapse despite respiratory effort, fragmenting sleep and desaturating blood. Central apnoea instead loses effort (neuromuscular or heart failure patterns). Obesity, male sex, advancing age, retrognathia, large neck circumference, nasal obstruction, adenotonsillar hypertrophy in children, alcohol and sedatives, and hypothyroidism or acromegaly cluster risk. Witnessed pauses, gasping arousals, unrefreshing sleep, morning headaches and daytime somnolence (Epworth scale) flag disease.
steps.say: Snore plus witnessed pauses plus sleepy days: obstructive apnoea until studied. Effort without air is obstruction; no effort is central.

steps.tx: Consequences reach beyond tiredness: intermittent hypoxia and sympathetic surges drive resistant hypertension, atrial fibrillation, stroke, nocturnal ischaemia, insulin resistance and road traffic or occupational accidents from microsleeps. **Polysomnography** quantifies apnoea hypopnoea index (AHI: events per hour; under 5 normal, 5 to 15 mild, 15 to 30 moderate, over 30 severe). Home testing suits uncomplicated high probability adults; complex, paediatric or cardiopulmonary cases need laboratory studies. Drug induced sleep endoscopy maps collapse levels (palate, tongue base, epiglottis) for surgical planning.
steps.say: Sleep apnoea grows blood pressure, arrhythmia and crashes. AHI over thirty is severe; study the complex in the lab.

steps.tx: **CPAP** splints the airway pneumatically and remains first line for moderate to severe adult OSA, improving sleepiness, blood pressure and accident risk when worn (adherence counselling, mask fitting, humidification and pressure titration decide success). Mandibular advancement devices suit mild to moderate disease or CPAP intolerance by protruding the jaw and tongue base. Weight loss, lateral or head up sleep, avoiding evening alcohol and sedatives, and treating nasal obstruction and hypothyroidism underpin every plan. Tracheostomy bypasses obstruction definitively but is reserved for life threatening refractory disease.
steps.say: CPAP pressure props the throat open nightly. Jaw devices and weight loss help mild disease; tracheostomy is the last resort bypass.

steps.tx: Surgery targets the mapped obstruction: **adenotonsillectomy** cures most paediatric OSA (Down syndrome or craniofacial cases need sleep studies first), while adults gain from tonsillectomy for massive tonsils, nasal surgery aiding CPAP tolerance, palatal procedures for selected collapse, tongue base or hyoid surgery, maxillomandibular advancement for skeletal deficiency, and hypoglossal nerve stimulation in CPAP failures meeting criteria. Perioperative vigilance matters because sedatives, opioids and supine recovery obstruct these airways; difficult airway and postoperative monitoring plans precede any anaesthetic.
steps.say: Big tonsils in snoring children come out first. Adult surgery follows the collapse map, never one operation for all.

rows: Surgery for mapped collapse or intolerance
